Ruled into OPS-16 as P-46 under amendment A-019 (VERIFIED at source: 90_operations/OPS-16_texas_market_plan_of_record.md line 116 carries 'P-46 ADDED: map layer controls - road nodes toggle defaulted OFF, and RRC layer toggles across its several layers').

The RRC grouping is REPORTED, not shipped, until the operator has seen it.

findingsAgainstTheBriefing.briefingSaid: 'The registry today carries rrc-wells, rrc-pipelines and texas-rrc as separate keys with different reach.'
findingsAgainstTheBriefing.sourceSays: There are TWO different registries and they do not overlap. The MAP LAYER registry (packages/map-renderer/src/layer-registry.js line 51) carries exactly ONE RRC key: { key: "texas-rrc", label: "Texas RRC O&G", group: "subsurface", fixture: false, live: false, fuelGated: false }. The keys rrc-wells and rrc-pipelines are COUNTY-LEDGER RAIL keys, declared at apps/command-center/src/admin/control/panels/countyManifestTypes.ts lines 142-143 ('rrc-wells': { label: 'RRC wells', short: 'WELL', kind: 'derived' } and 'rrc-pipelines': { label: 'RRC pipelines', short: 'PIPE', kind: 'derived' }). Neither string appears anywhere in packages/map-renderer.
findingsAgainstTheBriefing.consequence: The RRC work is not a regrouping of three existing map layers. It is a DECOMPOSITION of one inert map key into subjects that so far exist only as coverage rails. That is a bigger change than the briefing implies and it is the reason the grouping question is real.

findingsAgainstTheBriefing.severity: material - the layer draws nothing at all
findingsAgainstTheBriefing.finding: texas-rrc has NO data path in this repo. It has a registry row, a paint style (packages/map-renderer/src/map/gis-map-paint.js line 353), a stack position (same file line 474) and a CONTEXT role (packages/map-renderer/src/map/layer-role-taxonomy.js line 242) - and no fetch, no fixture, no API route. grep for 'rrc' across api/ and apps/property-explorer/api/ returns zero hits; live-gis.ts LiveLayerKey is 'parcels' | 'fema' | topo | hydro only; gis-fixture-data.js has no rrc slot.
findingsAgainstTheBriefing.consequence: On the SERVED layer, RRC coverage on the map today is zero everywhere, not 1 county. The 1-county ceiling is a property of the ingest source, not of anything a user can currently see. Any RRC toggle shipped now is a toggle over an empty set and must say so on its face.

findingsAgainstTheBriefing.finding: texas-rrc IS already listed as a live checkbox on Command Center and is NOT listed on Property Explorer. CC seeds known = the entire LAYER_REGISTRY (apps/command-center/src/admin/workspace/tiles/LiveMapTile.tsx lines 181-183). PE filters to live-wired rows only (apps/property-explorer/src/browse/consumer-layers.ts consumerKnownLayers), and texas-rrc has live:false and is not in the explicit keep-list, so it never renders a row there.
findingsAgainstTheBriefing.consequence: A CC operator can already tick 'Texas RRC O&G' today and get nothing, with no explanation. This is the exact defect work item 4 names, and it is live now, before any RRC grouping ships. It is not RRC-specific: six registry rows are fixture:false + live:false (ssurgo-soils, groundwater, mud-pid, edwards-aquifer, texas-rrc, etj) and all six behave this way on CC.

findingsAgainstTheBriefing.finding: There is no road-node toggle to default OFF; there is no toggle at all. apps/property-explorer/src/browse/road-overlay.ts sets 'visible: true' as a literal on the street ROW band spec (ROAD_ROW_BAND_LAYER_KEY) with no visibility parameter. Only the PEDESTRIAN child is switchable, via the existing registry key 'pedestrian-ways' (label 'Sidewalks / footpaths'), and that key is currently ON by default because consumerColdOpenVisible() turns on everything except zoning.
findingsAgainstTheBriefing.consequence: Work item 1 is an ADD (new registry key + wire + default), not a default flip.

rrcGroupingProposal.status: PROPOSED - NOT BUILT. Reported for operator decision per the dispatch instruction 'do not ship a structure the operator has not seen'.
rrcGroupingProposal.problemStatement: RRC is not one subject. Wells are points from a Harris-County endpoint mirror with a reachable ceiling of 1 county of 254. Pipelines are lines with no capability probe at all, so their ceiling is unknown rather than large. One toggle labelled 'Texas RRC O&G' makes those two facts invisible: a user turning it on over Midland and seeing nothing concludes there is no oil and gas in Midland, when what actually happened is that the well source only ever covered Harris.

optionsConsidered.option: A - keep one flat toggle 'Texas RRC O&G'
optionsConsidered.why: It is the status quo and it is the thing that asserts something false. It also cannot express two different denominators with one row.

optionsConsidered.option: B - two independent flat toggles, 'RRC wells' and 'RRC pipelines', texas-rrc retired
optionsConsidered.why: Honest and simple; each row carries its own reach. Costs the operator a single on/off for oil and gas, and puts two more rows in a panel that already runs long.

optionsConsidered.option: C - one parent row 'Texas RRC (oil & gas)' with indented children 'Wells' and 'Pipelines'
optionsConsidered.why: Gives the operator the one-click on/off he asked for without collapsing two different reaches into one claim. The parent is a control only and carries NO coverage language; every coverage statement lives on a child, where the denominator is real. Extends cleanly when a third RRC subject arrives.

rrcGroupingProposal.recommendation: Option C, with four conditions, none of them cosmetic
conditions: C1. The PARENT never states or implies coverage. It is a bulk on/off and a disclosure affordance. All reach language sits on children.

C2. Each CHILD carries its reachable ceiling with its denominator inline, and the ceiling's own timestamp. Proposed wells row secondary text: 'Wells - source reaches 1 of 254 counties (Harris mirror), as of 2026-08-14'. Proposed pipelines row: 'Pipelines - reachable ceiling unknown; no capability probe defined'. Unknown is written as unknown and never rendered as 254.

C3. Because neither child has a map data path today (F2), both ship as honest-empty rows: the checkbox works, and the row says what it would draw and why it currently draws nothing. A checkbox that silently does nothing is the defect, not the absence of data.

C4. texas-rrc is not deleted. It is RE-POINTED as the parent group id so its paint style, its stack slot at gis-map-paint.js line 474 and its CONTEXT role survive for the children, and no consumer breaks on a missing key.
rrcGroupingProposal.operatorDecisionNeeded: Approve C (parent + children), or fall back to B (two flat rows). Second question either way: should the RRC rows appear on Property Explorer at all, or stay Command-Center-only until a data path exists? This lane's recommendation is CC-only until then, because a consumer-facing row that can never draw anything is a support burden with no upside.
rrcGroupingProposal.notBuiltInThisLane: No RRC restructuring is in the branch. The only RRC-adjacent change shipped is the honest-empty treatment of work item 4, which makes the EXISTING inert texas-rrc row (and the other five inert rows) state their own emptiness.

adversarialReviewOfThisPlan: Risk: adding 'road-nodes' with live:true puts it in PE consumerKnownLayers automatically, and if COLD_OPEN_OFF_BY_DEFAULT is missed the operator gets the opposite of what he asked for. Mitigation: a test asserts the key is absent from consumerColdOpenVisible() and present in consumerKnownLayers(). The default is then enforced by a failing test rather than by care.

Risk: the street band currently paints unconditionally, so defaulting it OFF is a visible regression to anyone who liked seeing streets. That is exactly what the operator asked for ('defaulted to off for now'), and the satellite basemap still shows roads. Recorded so it is a decision, not a surprise.

Risk: LayersControl is shared, so a rendering change lands on CC without SS-W8 asking for it. Mitigation: additive only - no row disappears, no checkbox stops working, and the CC suite is run to confirm. No file under apps/command-center/** is edited.

Risk of the honest-empty mechanism itself: it reads registry status, so a layer that IS wired but happens to be declared live:false would be libelled as empty. Checked all six fixture:false+live:false rows; none has a fetch path in this repo. Stated as a constraint of the mechanism rather than assumed away.

What would make this plan wrong: if road-node street geometry is consumed by anything other than the PE map overlay - a report, an export - defaulting it off could starve that consumer. Checked: roadOverlaysFromAttachingRoads has exactly one non-test caller, ExplorerMap.tsx line 567, and it feeds the overlays array only. Render filter is not data filter; the twin still holds the geometry.
constraintsHonored: No sub-agents spawned; this lane is the deepest worker as instructed.
